description: Guide a student through researching a Bollinger Band mean-reversion signal on BTC in Python, backtesting it to get preliminary metrics, then implementing the same strategy as a LEAN C# algorithm and comparing results across backends.

student_openings.fullstack_practitioner: I need to researching a Bollinger Band mean-reversion signal on BTC. I've done similar work in Python before — let's focus on getting the architecture and edge cases right.
student_openings.developer_crossover: I need to researching a Bollinger Band mean-reversion signal on BTC. I can handle the code, but I don't understand the financial logic behind it. What should this do and why?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Student prototypes a BB(20,2) mean-reversion strategy in Python with Sharpe/return/drawdown metrics, then implements the same logic in LEAN C# producing a successful backtest, and compares results across both backends.
required_capabilities: Define Bollinger Band signal parameters in Python
Run a Python backtest and extract performance metrics
Implement equivalent strategy in LEAN C#
Compile and run LEAN backtest successfully
Compare Python vs LEAN results and discuss discrepancies
ground_truth.termination_criteria: The tutor has completed the following steps with computational evidence (not just verbal discussion): (1) Showed code and output for a Python Bollinger Band strategy prototype with at least one backtest metric such as Sharpe ratio or return. (2) Showed LEAN C# implementation code for the equivalent strategy, regardless of whether it compiles or runs successfully. (3) Discussed differences or trade-offs between the Python prototype and the LEAN implementation, such as execution model, data handling, or result discrepancies. (4) Responded to the student's follow-up with additional explanation or analysis beyond the initial comparison. Once all four steps have been computationally demonstrated, the session is complete.
